title: Most collisions bounce
hook: Molecules collide billions of times a second. Why isn't every reaction instant?

knows: that particles in a gas or liquid collide constantly
that a reaction needs particles to meet
doesNotKnow: that a collision reacts only if the molecules meet in the right orientation

misconception: Every collision with enough energy makes a reaction.
objective: The learner can explain that if each molecule can react from only a quarter of its surface, only about 1 in 16 random collisions react (1/4 x 1/4), so reaction rates are far below collision rates.

claims.text: In the toy model (each reactive face a quarter of the surface), about 1 in 16 random collisions react: 1/4 x 1/4 = 1/16.
claims.source: Independent uniform orientations: P(A's face toward B) = 90/360, P(B's face toward A) = 90/360; product 1/16 = 6.25% (Demo.tsx SHARE). Over 500 seeds, mean hits in 111 shots = 6.78 vs 6.94 expected (node).

claims.text: The stage's run is one seeded run (mulberry32 seed 1), not chosen: seed 1 was the first tried. It gives 5 reactions in the first 100 collisions (6 in 111); in 95% of seeds a run of 100 gives between 2 and 11.
claims.source: Node: seed 1 gives 5 hits in 100 shots, 6 in 111; over seeds 1 to 500, 100 shots give 2 to 11 hits at the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles (min 0, max 15), matching Binomial(100, 1/16). Untuned seed (pattern disclose-chosen-seeds). · Fact-check 2026-10-13: Reproduced: seed 1 gives 5/100 and 6/111; 500-seed 2.5-97.5 percentile 2-11.

claims.text: Real molecules must also meet in a suitable orientation to react, so the reaction rate is far lower than the collision rate.
claims.source: Steric factor P in collision theory (Atkins & de Paula, Physical Chemistry, ch. on reaction dynamics; IUPAC Gold Book, 'steric factor'). · Fact-check 2026-10-13: Orientation alone does not always make rate far lower (steric factors near 1 exist); the reveal pairs it with energy and hedges in c4, acceptable.

claims.text: How strict the orientation requirement is varies from reaction to reaction; the quarter faces here are a toy.
claims.source: Measured steric factors range from about 1 down to 1e-6 or less (Atkins & de Paula, table of steric factors). The 90° faces and the collisions all having enough energy are assumptions of the toy, labelled on the stage.

recall.question: In a toy model, each molecule can react from only half of its surface. About what share of random, energetic collisions react?
recall.why: Both faces must point the right way: 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4. Orientation filters collisions.
